summary: Hard for AI agents that read messages, even though creating the app is self-serve. Slack's 2025 terms make the Marketplace the only approved channel for commercial distribution. Unlisted commercial apps are limited to 1 request per minute (15 messages) on conversations.history and conversations.replies. Marketplace listing needs 10 active workspace installs and a review of up to about 10 weeks. Build and test in your own workspace now, and plan the Marketplace submission early.

oauth_support_claim.text: Slack apps install via OAuth 2.0 (Slack 'V2' OAuth with granular bot and user scopes).
oauth_support_claim.quote: you must upgrade your OAuth flow to use the Slack V2 of OAuth 2.0

difficulty_claim.text: The app itself is self-serve, but commercial distribution outside the Marketplace runs at Tier 1 rate limits for message history. Marketplace approval has install prerequisites and a multi-week review.
difficulty_claim.quote: the Slack Marketplace is the only appropriate channel for commercially distributing apps built with Slack APIs
difficulty_claim.note: Often listed as 'moderate'. This guide rates it hard for agents that read conversations. Write-only bots and apps used only inside your own company are closer to moderate.

claim.text: Composio names Slack among toolkits with a Composio-managed OAuth app.
claim.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack.
claim.note: Not checked: whether Composio's managed Slack app is Marketplace-listed, which decides the rate limits your users get.

endpoints.note: Standard Slack V2 OAuth endpoints. Slack refused our automated requests (HTTP 403), so they were not tested live.

hands_on.text: 20-45 minutes to a working app in your own workspace
hands_on.note: Estimated: create the app, add scopes, set the redirect URL, enable distribution, install.

approval_wait.text: Marketplace: preliminary review up to 10 business days, then functional review up to 10 weeks. You first need 10 active workspace installs.
approval_wait.quote: the functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions
approval_wait.note: In the preliminary stage your place in the queue resets each time you resubmit.

fastest_path.text: Internal apps in your own workspace keep normal rate limits (50+ requests/min, 1,000 messages). Unlisted distribution works right away for development and pilots.
fastest_path.quote: Internal customer-built applications are not impacted by these changes

steps.title: Create an app at api.slack.com/apps (from a manifest if you like)
steps.detail: Pick a development workspace. A manifest (YAML/JSON) keeps scopes and redirect URLs in code, so you can keep a staging copy in sync.
steps.quote: You can create a copy of your app for dev/staging using your published app’s manifest.

steps.title: Choose minimal bot/user scopes
steps.detail: List the API methods you call and pick only their scopes. Prefer bot tokens. Avoid legacy and broad scopes that the Marketplace rejects (e.g. admin.*, search:read, identity.*).
steps.quote: use only the absolute minimum number of scopes for your app to work

steps.title: Add the redirect URL from Composio and enable public distribution
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions > Redirect URLs: paste your Composio callback. Manage Distribution > activate public distribution so other workspaces can install.
steps.note: Standard Slack console flow. Not walked by the agent (HTTP 403).

steps.title: Install to your workspace and test
steps.detail: Install, connect through Composio, and check the token types and scopes you receive.

phases.name: Reach 10 active workspaces
phases.summary: Required before you can submit to the Marketplace.

steps.title: Get design partners to install the unlisted app
steps.detail: 10 or more workspaces must be active in the past 28 days. Expect Tier 1 limits on history and replies for these new installs.
steps.quote: Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces

phases.name: Marketplace review
phases.summary: Weeks. Your live app is locked once listed.

steps.title: Prepare the listing, test accounts and a demo video
steps.detail: Reviewers need a way to install the app themselves and test credentials (with dummy data) for your service. A video of install, OAuth, setup, use and uninstall speeds review.
steps.why_human: Test accounts and the recording come from you.
steps.quote: provide us with test account credentials needed to access your service
steps.note: An agent can draft the listing copy and the video script.

steps.title: Submit and answer feedback
steps.detail: Preliminary review is up to 10 business days, functional review up to 10 weeks for new apps. You cannot pay or ask to speed it up.
steps.why_human: Submission and responses come from the app owner.
steps.quote: We are unable to skip or accelerate the review process

steps.title: Keep a staging app for future scope changes
steps.detail: Once you are listed, adding scopes needs a new review, and new scopes do not work until approved.
steps.quote: the live version of your app is locked

requirements.title: 10 active workspace installs before Marketplace submission
requirements.detail: Active means used in the past 28 days. Apps below this cannot submit.
requirements.quote: apps that do not meet this requirement will be blocked from submitting to the Marketplace

requirements.title: HTTPS redirect URL
requirements.note: Not verified against Slack docs in this pass.

gotchas.title: 1 request/minute on conversations.history and replies for unlisted commercial apps
gotchas.detail: Apps created after May 29, 2025, and new installs of older unlisted apps, get Tier 1 limits with at most 15 objects per call. Agents that summarize channels will stall.
gotchas.quote: The new rate limits will be updated to allow 1 request per minute and will return a maximum of 15 objects per request.

gotchas.title: Resubmitting resets your place in the queue
gotchas.detail: During preliminary review, each resubmission starts the timeline over. Read the guidelines before you submit.
gotchas.quote: your place in the queue is reset each time you resubmit

gotchas.title: Marketplace rejects scopes for unbuilt features
gotchas.detail: Only request scopes for features reviewers can test now.
gotchas.quote: Please do not submit your app with scopes for a feature that you plan to build at some point in future.

blockers.title: Reading message history at scale without a listing
blockers.detail: Tier 1 limits make bulk reading impractical for new commercial installs.
blockers.workaround: Use the Events API for new messages instead of polling history. Run it as an internal app per customer only if your terms allow. Ask about the Real-time Search API (limited partner beta).
blockers.quote: consider the other ways the platform may provide to get the kind of focused, contextual information an app typically requires, such as the Events API

blockers.title: Some app types are not accepted on the Marketplace
blockers.detail: Coded workflows are not eligible, and Slack lists other excluded categories.
blockers.workaround: Check the guidelines before building around a listing.
blockers.quote: Coded workflows are currently not eligible for listing in the Slack Marketplace.

Install to workspaces and recruit 10 active workspaces
Provide reviewers with test accounts, submit, and answer feedback

conflicts.positions: Slack's changelog says existing installs of unlisted apps keep their limits. A third-party issue tracker says existing installs became subject to the limits on March 3, 2026.
conflicts.resolution: Unresolved. Check Slack's latest changelog. The official page we fetched does not mention a 2026 date.

unknowns: Whether Composio's managed Slack app is Marketplace-listed (which decides its rate limits).
Current actual review times; Slack shows an estimate on the submission page.
